title: Design a Parking Garage System
prompt: Design a parking garage system that tracks available spots across multiple levels, assigns a spot to an arriving vehicle (with different spot sizes for motorcycles/cars/buses), and frees the spot when the vehicle leaves.
requirements: Functional: check in a vehicle (assign an appropriate spot), check out a vehicle (free its spot), query available spot counts by type
Non-functional: fast spot lookup even with thousands of spots, correct behavior with concurrent check-ins from multiple entrances
discussion_points: Data model for levels, spots, and spot sizes/types
Assignment strategy (nearest available, by type) and how to keep lookups fast
Concurrency: two vehicles arriving at the same time shouldn't be assigned the same spot
This is a smaller-scale problem — is a single-service, single-database design good enough, and why?
How you'd extend this to multiple garages/locations
